subject: Service continuity annex / order-form appendix for OrionThera
body:
---- Message 1 (2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00) ----
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@orionthera.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@orionthera.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service continuity annex / order-form appendix for OrionThera

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to pull together the availability/uptime language we need to close the MSA + order form. A few things we need explicit clarity on before we circulate to legal:

- Minimum monthly availability target for production (we're trying to understand options between 99.95% vs 99.99%).
- P99 latency guarantees for API generation (we run interactive tools, so tails matter).
- What operational evidence you'll provide on onboarding (SLA dashboard snapshots, sample logs, SOC2 references).
- Acceptable maintenance/upgrade windows and the notification process for planned downtime.

Can you share a draft exhibit + a short list of what artifacts Redwood can produce at sign (and post-sign cadence)? Also, we'll need a DocuSign-ready SOW + order form appendix with the chosen SLA numbers called out.

Best,
Alice
Senior Procurement Manager
OrionThera

---- Message 2 (2027-04-26T10:04:00-07:00) ----
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@orionthera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service continuity annex / order-form appendix for OrionThera

Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching a first-pass draft we call the "Service Safeguard Annex" (attached) and a short checklist that maps deliverables to signing milestones. High-level proposals below so legal/procurement can react:

- Baseline monthly availability: 99.95% (standard). Option A (premium): 99.99% for an additional usage uplift in the order form; we'd include a schedule of monthly credits for missed targets.
- Latency commitment: P99 <= 400ms for text-generation endpoints for region us-west-2 under the provisioned capacity profile in the order form. For burst/ondemand paths we provide best-effort and declare a different latency band.
- Evidence at signing: SOC 2 Type II summary, sample 7-day SLA dashboard export (CSV/PNG), and an annotated runbook describing maintenance cadence. Post-sign cadence: weekly dashboard exports for first 60 days, then monthly.
- Maintenance: maintenance windows limited to 3 hours per maintenance event, windows scheduled with minimum 7-day notice for routine maintenance; emergency maintenance has a separate notification and rollback protocol.

Ben and Marissa — looping you for legal/implementation language we should include in the annex (credits formula, exclusions, and the order form appendix fields to make billing deterministic).

Next steps: I can turn the attached docx into a DocuSign-ready SOW package by Friday if that timing works for you.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_service_safeguard_annex_v1.docx, orion-proofing-checklist.xlsx

---- Message 3 (2027-04-27T09:37:00-07:00) ----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Alice Wong <alice.wong@orionthera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service continuity annex / order-form appendix for OrionThera

Thanks, Diego. Quick legal notes after an initial pass of the annex:

- Credits: propose a straightforward pro rata credit calculation tied to total monthly fees (not per-API-call) to keep it auditable: credit = (monthly fee) * (downtime minutes / total minutes in month) * credit multiplier. We'll propose multipliers that scale by the SLA band (higher multiplier for missed 99.99%).
- Exclusions: maintenance compliant with the notice provisions, force majeure, and customer-caused issues (e.g., misuse, misconfiguration) should be explicit.
- Evidence: we can state Redwood will provide dashboard exports and log extracts, but redact PII where present. If Orion requires raw syslogs, that triggers an evidence-collection addendum and further review.
- Termination for SLA failure: avoid automatic termination for a single missed month; instead propose termination rights only after 3 non-consecutive failing months within a rolling 12-month period.

I’ve added comments inline on the draft (see docx). Happy to iterate.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---- Message 4 (2027-04-29T11:20:00-07:00) ----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@orionthera.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service continuity annex / order-form appendix for OrionThera

Hi Alice —

Operational notes from a CS/Onboarding perspective to include in the exhibit:

- Canary & rollout: we'll require a short canary window (48–72 hours) for new production model variants. Canary traffic will be routed to a segregated baseline pool; rollback is executed automatically on regressions we observe per the baseline metric set.
- Monitoring hooks: we will provide a webhook to Orion's PagerDuty/Datadog for uptime events and a service-level dashboard link with tokenized read-only view.
- Runbook handover: we'll schedule a 90-minute ops workshop at handover plus a 30-day health check.
- Proof-of-concept evidence: we can produce a 7-day sampled dataset showing p99 and uptime under load run on a representative workload — this is the sla-metrics-sample.png attached.

If Orion prefers the 99.99% band, we'll need to lock in dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in the order form and confirm the billing uplift. I included a short worksheet in the checklist to model monthly costs.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-metrics-sample.png

---- Message 5 (2027-04-30T16:45:00-07:00) ----
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@orionthera.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@orionthera.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service continuity annex / order-form appendix for OrionThera

Diego/Marissa/Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. A few action items from our side after an internal read:

1) Procurement is comfortable starting with 99.95% baseline. We are going to request pricing for the 99.99% reserved-capacity option as a line item in the order form — please include the uplift worksheet in the DocuSign package.
2) Legal will review Ben's comments; if we ask for raw syslogs we'll follow up and expect a scoping conversation.
3) We need the DocuSign-ready SOW + the final Service Safeguard Annex by EOD next Wednesday (2027-05-05) so our legal and security teams can complete vendor review before the executive signature.
4) Also: can you attach a short (1-page) note describing the mechanics of credits calculation so our finance team can ingest it into our template?

If you can deliver the revised docx + DocuSign link and the 1-pager proof note by Wednesday, we'll schedule the final signature the following week.

I'll confirm internally and loop in security if they want the raw-log ask pursued.

Best,
Alice Wong
Senior Procurement Manager
OrionThera

Attachments referenced: draft_service_safeguard_annex_v1.docx, orion-proofing-checklist.xlsx, sla-metrics-sample.png
